sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-full/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 39 (check 38), Deterministic Checks row 5 (check-batched-independence-wording.py), Internal Quality Checks row 39 (check 38, no reviewer annotation on this row)
evidence: All three scored dimensions (scoring.toml weights functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2; each judge.toml mode="batched", aggregation="weighted_mean"; 43, 6 and 3 criteria) carry explicit independence-and-continue wording: functional/prompt.md:13 "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure; return a verdict for every criterion. A failed criterion never ends the session." plus :12 "a failure in one must not fail another whose own steps passed" and :28 "give every criterion its own verdict"; polish/prompt.md:12-13 same sentence plus "Never carry a verdict across criteria"; visual/prompt.md:15 "Score each criterion independently and continue after any failure or low score; return a score for every criterion ... never carry a score across criteria". No scored prompt tells the judge to stop at the first failure: the only 'stop' rules are per-criterion (functional:17 "stop and fail that criterion, then continue with the rest"; functional:29, polish:22, visual:23 "retry once, then fail that criterion and move on"), and the shared checker-not-fixer paragraph ends "move on to the next criterion". The only all-or-nothing rule is the render precondition (prompt line 5, 'the only all-or-nothing rule in this dimension'), which is a load floor, not a first-miss cascade. A grep of the scored judge.toml criteria for references to other criteria's outcomes found none ('stop' hits at functional judge.toml:128/254/290/308 are in-step instructions); cross-criterion setup is self-contained and app_context.md:32 states criteria not needing Run are scored on their own steps. Gate dimensions (render, constraints) use aggregation="all_pass" and are exempt. Wording matches the template's scored-prompt intent (template functional/prompt.md:68, polish/visual 'Independent scoring' sections). Counterexample attempts: a broken app whose Run fails still gets per-criterion verdicts on editor/keyboard criteria (no cascade); a conforming app that fails one criterion cannot have later criteria zeroed by wording. Residual (owned by other rows, not this one): the functional prompt:14 rule marking unattempted criteria failed on budget exhaustion is a workload/timeout concern for the workload rows, not a stop-on-first-failure instruction; no configured-judge run exists for v16 bytes (raw-evidence-index scope), and I did not execute check-batched-independence-wording.py (not present in the frozen rules), which the deterministic reviewer owns.
